zh: 圆圈里出现的身高一定是一段连续的整数；如果圈里同时有最低和最高身高，中间的每个身高都要在圆圈的两条弧上各出现一次，所以至少要有两个人，两端的身高可以只有一个人。
统计每个身高的人数，问题变成找一段连续身高区间：内部每个身高至少 2 人、两端至少 1 人，使总人数最大。对每个左端，最远能延伸到第一个人数不超过 1 的身高处。
用前缀和求区间人数，从大到小预处理每个身高之后第一个人数 ≤1 的位置。枚举有人的左端 l，设该位置为 stop：若 stop 处恰有 1 人，右端取 stop，否则取 stop−1；记录总人数最大的区间。输出时先从低到高每个身高放一个人，再从高到低放剩下的所有人。
en: The heights in a circle always form a range of consecutive integers. If the circle contains both its lowest and highest heights, every height in between must appear once on each of the two arcs, so it needs at least two people; the two end heights may have just one.

Count people per height. The task becomes finding a range of consecutive heights where every inner height has at least 2 people and both ends have at least 1, maximizing the total. For each left end, the range can reach as far as the first later height with at most 1 person.

Use prefix sums for range totals, and precompute, scanning from high to low, the first height after each height whose count is at most 1. For each occupied left end l with that position stop: the right end is stop if exactly one person has height stop, otherwise stop−1; keep the range with the largest total. To output, place one person of each height going up, then all remaining people going down.

explanationEn:
## Approach

In a usable contiguous range of heights, every inner height must have at least two people, while the two endpoints may have only one. Use prefix sums of the frequencies and the next position whose frequency is ≤1 to find the largest range, then take one person of each height in ascending order and output the remaining people in descending order.

## Proof of correctness

If a circle contains both the minimum and the maximum height, every height in between must appear once on each of the two different paths around the circle; otherwise one could not go from low to high and come back. Conversely, when every inner frequency is at least 2, going up once in ascending order and then coming back down through the remaining people in descending order builds a valid circle. For each left end, the farthest valid right end is determined by the first position with frequency ≤1, and since frequencies are positive, taking the farthest is optimal; enumerating the left ends gives the maximum number of people.

## Complexity

Time O(n+V), space O(n+V), where V is the largest height.
